reason: Bricks and metal stock seem like useful structural materials for a place to sit and work, so I’ll start with them.
expectation: I expect them to make a support or frame, though I’m unsure what form it will take.

alternatives.reason: Felt and fabric might make a cushion, but a supporting structure seems useful first.

effect: The bricks and metal made a bench with a seat and worktop, so it now seems useful to make a softer covering for it.
reaction: The reuse of the workshop materials is satisfying.
reason: Felt and fabric seem suited to a cushion, and this is the only offered combination.
expectation: I expect them to make a padded cover or cushion, though I don’t know its exact form.

effect: The felt and fabric made the expected cushion, which can now go on the bench.
reaction: The result was predictable, but it makes practical sense.
reason: Putting the cushion on the bench is the only offered combination and should finish the seating area.
expectation: I expect a cushioned window bench and possibly completion of the goal.

effect: The cushion completed the window bench and the goal, providing both a worktop and a place to sit.
reaction: The image of watching the sunset from the padded bench is a satisfying payoff.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making the bare bench was most worthwhile: the bricks and metal became both a seat and a worktop, giving familiar materials a useful new purpose.

leastWorthwhile.text: Making the cushion was the least distinctive passage; its result was predictable and had no further description.

surprise.text: The bench structure also included a worktop, which gave it a clearer working purpose than I had expected.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt arbitrary. The materials and their uses were clear, although the last two combinations were the only ones offered at their respective steps.

continue.text: I would choose to continue, mainly to see how life in the cabin and the expedition develop. This chapter was pleasant, though its combinations involved little uncertainty.
